outcome: No resolution, partial resolution, or bound-moving progress was found for the classical Sato-Tate conjecture or its stated generalizations since 26 January 2024; the classical elliptic-curve case was already proved in 2008-2011 (pre-window), and the active literature since the cutoff consists of case-by-case Sato-Tate group computations for specific curve/abelian-variety families and adjacent variant problems, none of which resolves a stated general conjecture.
summary: The Wikipedia bullet groups the classical Sato-Tate conjecture with 'a number of related conjectures that are generalizations of the original.' The classical case (elliptic curves over totally real fields, non-CM) was proved by Taylor, Barnet-Lamb, Clozel, Geraghty, Harris et al. in 2008-2011, well before the 26 Jan 2024 frozen revision, so that part of the bullet is already open_stale territory rather than something that moved in the window -- but since the bullet is explicitly about the generalizations still open beyond that classical case, I classify the whole bullet as 'open' rather than 'open_stale', since the stated open content (the generalizations) remains open. I independently verified via direct fetches (not just the triage's snippets) that: (1) arXiv:2412.02522 (Goodson-Hoque, submitted 3 Dec 2024) computes the Sato-Tate group/distribution for one specific curve family y^l = x(x^l-1) -- a case-level computation in the ongoing Fite-Kedlaya-Sutherland-style classification program, not a resolution of any general conjecture; (2) arXiv:2507.02535 (Gallese-Goodson-Lombardo, submitted 3 Jul 2025) explicitly states 'there is no general algorithm that computes this invariant' and computes the Sato-Tate group for one specific hyperelliptic Jacobian family plus a structural extension to degenerate abelian varieties -- again a special case, not a general resolution; (3) the live Wikipedia article (fetched directly) still states 'Several generalizations to other algebraic varieties and fields are open' and contains no mention of any 2024-2026 development, and its edit history in that window shows only bot/gnome citation and link maintenance, no substantive content edits. A genuinely major result, Boxer-Calegari-Gee-Newton-Thorne's proof of the Ramanujan and Sato-Tate conjectures for GL(2) automorphic representations over CM fields (arXiv:2309.15880), is the strongest candidate for in-window progress: I fetched the arXiv page directly and confirmed v1 was submitted 27 Sep 2023 (before the cutoff), but the paper was revised to its 'accepted version' on 6 Nov 2024, published online in Forum of Mathematics, Pi (DOI 10.1017/fmp.2024.29, vol. 13, e10) on 21 Feb 2025, and corrected again (v3) on 27 Mar 2025 -- all inside the window. Per the dating rule (date the first public written argument, i.e. the preprint, not the journal publication), the decisive event predates the frozen revision, so this does not count as in-window progress on this bullet, and I record no event. I also checked Terence Tao's blog (his own site search returned zero Sato-Tate posts) and searched for Quanta Magazine coverage (none found; Sato-Tate does not appear on Quanta's 2024 or 2025 year-in-math lists) -- both negative results supporting that nothing reached expert-digestion or general press attention in the window. I found no AI/LLM involvement anywhere: no AlphaProof/AlphaEvolve/GPT/Copilot/Claude connection to any Sato-Tate paper, and the one existing AI-Sato-Tate connection ('Machine-learning the Sato-Tate conjecture,' He-Lee-Oliver, J. Symbolic Computation vol. 111, 2022) predates the window by two years. A thematically adjacent but distinct AI paper, 'Learning Euler Factors of Elliptic Curves' (arXiv:2502.10357, Feb 2025), uses transformers to predict Frobenius traces a_p but does not itself engage the Sato-Tate conjecture as a mathematical statement.
competing_reading: One could argue the bullet should be split: the classical elliptic-curve case is 'open_stale' (settled 2008-2011, before the frozen revision) while the generalizations are 'open' with no change, and a stricter reading might also argue the Boxer-Calegari-Gee-Newton-Thorne CM-field result, since its acceptance and formal publication fall inside the window, should be recorded as an 'event' with status 'resolved' (a genuine unconditional resolution of the Ramanujan/Sato-Tate conjectures for GL(2) over CM fields, a real generalization of the classical statement) even though its preprint predates the cutoff, on the grounds that this is exactly the kind of generalization the bullet's own text points to. I judged the dating rule (§6.3: date the first public written argument, i.e. the preprint) to control here, and the preprint's substantive mathematical content (v1, Sep 2023) predates the window with only editorial/acceptance changes occurring later, so I did not record it as an event; a reader who weighs the journal-publication date more heavily could reasonably classify this bullet as 'resolved' or 'partial' instead of 'open'.
what_would_settle_it: Whether the Boxer-Calegari-Gee-Newton-Thorne result's Nov 2024 'accepted version' revision constituted a new substantive written argument (as opposed to purely editorial changes from peer review) would settle whether it should be dated inside the window; checking the diff between v1 and v2 on arXiv, or Frank Calegari's own account of the timeline (e.g. on his blog, if any), would clarify this.
